Completed two-way table: males who watch TV during exams $80$, males who do not $a$, row total $80+a$; females $48$ and $12$, row total $60$; column totals $b$ and $32$; grand total $160$.

$a+12=32$, so $a=20$.

$b=80+48=128$.

We want to create codes that are even numbers greater than $5000$. The digit $6$ can be used in one of two places in these codes and therefore this presents two scenarios.

CASE $1$: The first digit is a $6$.

$1\times 5\times 4\times 2=40$

Number of codes starting with $6$ $=40$.

CASE $2$: The first digit is a $5$ or $7$.

$2\times 5\times 4\times 3=120$

Number of codes not starting with $6$ $=120$.

Therefore total number of possible codes $=40+120=160$.
